working_title: The Tied Arm That Proved Your Blood Circulates
title: The Liver That Made Blood

chapter_card.treatment: soft cross-fade after the last word + 0.6 s breath; music continues

open_stamp.treatment: Didot italic side label in the edit

set_language: Warm candlelit 17th-century world: dark oak, cream linen, brass, leather books, London fog. Body cutaways are clean, glowing illustrations (warm red arteries, cool blue veins), never anatomical gore. Say 'same 1616 London lecture room' or 'same Harvey study' for continuity; never 'same DNA'.
explorer_lock: ONE beat (plate 13): the Explorer on the top rail of the empty Padua anatomy theatre, traces the little doors on Fabricius's drawing, then slips away. Attach 01_Character/05_Generation-References/hos-explorer-reference-v01.jpg.
forbidden: HARD REJECT: Orbit robot; photoreal; Ken Burns or still push; gore, wounds, blood on skin, cut flesh or real animal organs (animal hearts only as Harvey's ink drawings); live or dead animals on a table; lava drip / molten bead; underside lamp bulb or shade cup; unfinished flat cards; garbled writing; unfinished Explorer hair; DNA helix; readable text or logos baked into the plate (labels and the De Motu Cordis title are added in the edit); twin Explorer; faces in the first two seconds of the film. Never say 'same DNA' or 'lab DNA' in a Veo prompt.
always_fails: garbled card text or wrong sums (2 oz, 1/8, 1000 checked by hand)
unfinished Explorer hair or melted face
gore: wound, blood on skin, cut flesh, real animal organs
a face in the first two seconds of the film
motion_lock: Real Veo camera and object motion on every plate. No freeze-pad, no loop, no Ken Burns.
quality_note: Flow Veo 3.1 on the Mac Mini CDP worker, benoats@googlemail.com only. Quality for anything with light (candles, glowing loop, stove heart) and every hero plate; Fast only for low-risk garnish. One plate at a time until the first KEEP; after 2 same-framing FAILs change the framing.
labels: White Didot italic side label, 1-4 words, one at a time, on the plate's first beat; added in the edit.

plates.vo_land: Galen was a Greek doctor in Rome nearly two thousand years ago, and a brilliant anatomist.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Rome around AD 170, a lamplit study full of scroll racks: Galen, a Greek doctor of about fifty, curly grey hair and beard, cream Greek robe, writes on a scroll with a reed pen; the oil lamp glows cleanly. Camera drifts in. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: For fourteen centuries, hardly anyone dared to argue with his books.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Galen's scrolls become heavy leather books down the centuries: shelves fill with copies, monks and then gowned doctors bow over them by candlelight. A continuous slow pan through time. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. A warm, clean cartoon cutaway of a seated person, simple glowing outline of the body: they take a bite of bread and a soft milky glow travels down into the belly. Friendly, clear, no anatomy gore. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Your food turns into a milky juice, and your liver turns that juice into blood.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same cutaway body. The milky stream flows into a smooth stylised liver, which glows and turns it warm red. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Your veins carry the blood out to every part of you, and your flesh soaks it up as nourishment.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same cutaway body. Warm red streams flow out along the veins into the arms and legs and fade away into the flesh like water into sand. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: The heart wasn't a pump at all.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same cutaway body. The heart glows like a little iron stove with a soft warm fire inside, warming the red blood that seeps slowly past it. Clean warm glow, no flames spitting. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: A little of it was meant to seep from the right side of the heart to the left, through tiny holes in the wall between them.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. A cutaway cartoon heart: a few red drops creep from the right side to the left through tiny imagined pores in the wall between the two sides; the pores flicker as if not really there. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Nobody had ever seen those holes.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. A candlelit room of gowned doctors around a chart of the heart with dotted holes drawn in its wall; they nod and point confidently at the holes nobody has seen. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Then, in fifteen fifty-five, the great anatomist Andreas Vesalius wrote that he could not see how even the smallest drop could pass through that wall.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. A great anatomy book lies open on a woodcut-style drawing of the heart (no readable text); a brass magnifying glass slides across the wall between its two sides by candlelight. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: (+6.5 s into) Then, in fifteen fifty-five, the great anatomist Andreas Vesalius wrote that he could not see how even the smallest drop could pass through that wall.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same open book. Through the magnifying glass the heart wall is solid and smooth: a single tiny drop of red ink beads against it and cannot pass. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: So why did everyone keep believing it?
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Galen's thick book on a lectern; students keep copying from it by candlelight as the candle burns down. Camera drifts. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Around sixteen hundred, in Padua, a young Englishman named William Harvey studied under an old professor called Fabricius.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Padua around 1600: the steep wooden oval anatomy theatre, rings of carved rails rising around a small table, candlelit and empty. Camera rises slowly up the rails. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: (+5.0 s into) Around sixteen hundred, in Padua, a young Englishman named William Harvey studied under an old professor called Fabricius.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same Padua anatomy theatre. Exactly ONE Explorer, on model: a young boy, messy wavy brown hair (full crown), round thin gold glasses, long teal coat, tan waistcoat, brown bow tie, satchel. He acts, then leaves. He climbs to the top rail, looks down at the candlelit table, unrolls a drawing of a vein on the rail and traces its tiny paired flaps with one finger, then slips away into the shadows. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame.

plates.vo_land: Fabricius had found something strange inside the veins: tiny flaps, in pairs.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same Padua theatre. Fabricius, an old Italian professor, long white beard, black scholar's cap and robe, holds up a large drawing of a vein opened along its length, candlelight on his face. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Fabricius's drawing comes alive: a vein opened along its length, pairs of tiny flaps inside like little doors gently swinging. Warm parchment and ink look, no readable text. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Fabricius thought they slowed the blood, so it wouldn't all pool in your feet.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Same living drawing: a faint red trickle runs down a leg vein and the little doors catch it, holding it back from pooling in the foot, as Fabricius imagined. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: He held the most important clue in the story, and he read it the wrong way.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Padua study by candlelight: young William Harvey, about twenty-two, olive skin, black hair, first thin beard, dark keen eyes, dark student's gown, studies Fabricius's vein drawing closely, frowns, then rolls it up carefully. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Harvey took the clue home to London.
plates.prompt: Premium Animistry-class 3D cartoon. Young Harvey with the rolled drawing under his arm walks up the gangplank of a wooden sailing ship at a misty dawn harbour; sails fill. Silent. Continuous motion through the final frame. No Explorer.
